notes: Summary: Veridian builds a legal knowledge platform used by UK/EU law firms and in-house counsels. Strong constraint: vectors + derived embeddings must remain in-region (UK or EU) for contractual clients. Primary interest: low-latency semantic search over 100M+ documents with reranking for precision.
Scale targets: initial index 50M docs (contracts, briefs), long-term target 200M+ docs; estimated vector store ~18TB compressed; expected 500-1,500 QPS for peak product searches.

Performance SLOs: p95 end-to-end search latency < 200ms (goal), preferred p95 < 120ms for interactive use-cases. Reranker budget target: add < 60ms p95 to maintain UX. Cost sensitivity: target <= €0.003/query average across hybrid retrieval+rerank.

Current architecture ask: hybrid retrieval (sparse + ANN) -> 100 candidate recall -> cross-encoder rerank for top 10. Want Redwood to support two-tier routing: EU primary (eu-west), UK-resident pool for UK-only customers, automatic multi-region failover to read-only cold replicas.

POC results (initial): ANN (HNSW) retrieval median 35-50ms; cross-encoder rerank on CPU baseline adds 90-140ms -> total p95 ~220ms. Priya suggested kernel-level quantization + dedicated GPU reranker to hit 120ms p95. Redwood Optimize recommended batching + KV prefix caching to save ~18% token cost.
Quotes: 'We can't have vectors leaving the UK for a subset of clients — contract will fail otherwise.' — Head of InfoSec (Veridian).

Legal/compliance: Veridian legal team requires a written data residency SLA + audit trail for all index operations. Also needs KMS integration with existing Azure Key Vault and proof of no export outside selected region.

Ops/Infra asks: autoscaling for peak research hours, warm standby in secondary EU region for failover, optional cold-read replicas for analytics; prefer ability to pin model versions and control quantization profiles per index.

Cost considerations: finance wants modeled spend at 1k QPS -> estimate 600k/month raw; exploring Dedicated reserved commit vs. Private on-prem for most sensitive customers. Looking for Redwood to provide detailed cost-per-query breakdown by retrieval vs. rerank.
